spatial_claims.claim: ABC is an equilateral triangle constructed on segment AB (I.1); D is the midpoint of AB; CD is drawn
Triangles ADC and BDC are congruent by SSS (AD=DB, AC=BC, CD common), so angles ADC and BDC are equal
Angles ADC and BDC are adjacent angles on line AB that are equal, hence both are right angles
Triangle ADC is right-angled at D, so Q(AC) = Q(AD) + Q(CD) by I.47
AC = AB because triangle ABC is equilateral, so Q(AB) = Q(AD) + Q(CD)
AB = 2·AD (D is midpoint), so Q(AB) = 4·Q(AD), giving Q(CD) = 3·Q(AD)

configuration_map: Points: A, B are endpoints of the given rational line. C is the apex of equilateral triangle ABC, above line AB. D is the midpoint of segment AB. Line CD is the altitude/perpendicular bisector of the equilateral triangle, meeting AB at right angles at D. Triangle ADC is a right triangle with right angle at D, hypotenuse AC = AB, and legs AD = AB/2, CD = AB·sqrt(3)/2. All spatial relationships are standard properties of an equilateral triangle and its altitude. No point changes position or role across steps.
